text.p: Apple Computer Inc Tuesday said it is consolidating the company's product development, marketing, sales support and operations efforts into groups that will focus on core businesses.
In a statement, Apple also said former co-founders Steve Jobs and Steve Wozniak will be reunited as advisors to Chairman Gilbert Amelio and serve on Apple's Executive Committee.
The company said some jobs would be eliminated by the restructuring but it did not provide specifics.
Industry analysts said they expect Apple to cut between 2,000 and 3,000 jobs from its workforce of around 13,000 employees.

"We are reshaping our product development, sales, and marketing efforts into simpler, leaner teams that can quickly bring exceptional products to market -- and then aggressively market them to customers in our key markets," Amelio said. "The organization and team we're announcing today represent the right people, in the right places, to bring Apple back to its basics and return us to profitability by the end of the fiscal year."
Apple did not say what it plans to do with its Newton personal digital assistant, which analysts said Apple may decide to sell.

Apple, once the darling of the computer industry, has suffered in recent years from missed opportunities, management turmoil and failed strategies that resulted in the departures of John Sculley in 1993 and Michael Spindler three years later. Experts say Apple's decision not to license the Macintosh operating system to other manufacturers allowed rival Microsoft Corp to catch up with its Windows operating system.

By the time Apple reversed course, more than 80 percent of the world's computers were using Windows, making it difficult for Apple to make inroads even though many computer enthusiasts felt Apple's system was easier to use.
Compounding Apple's woes were a series of production and forecasting problems which prevented Apple from capitalizing on the PC buying craze and the popularity of the Internet.
In its statement, Apple said it plans to integrate its development resources with those of NeXT Software Inc, which Apple acquired for $400 million. NeXT was founded by Steve Jobs.
Under Apple's restructuring plan, Ellen Hancock will continue to head up the technology office.
The company's product development will be consolidated into two groups, one focusing on system software engineering and the other on hardware engineering.

System software will be led by NeXT's Avie Tevanian while hardware engineering will be led by Jon Rubinstein, formerly chief operating officer of FirePower Systems Inc. For the first time in Apple's history, marketing operations will be consolidated into a single organization headed by Guerrino De Luca, formerly the head of Apple's Claris unit.
Apple said Marco Landi will head Apple's new worldwide sales and support organization and its finance department will continue to be led by chief finanical officer Fred Anderson.

Apple said the new organization will define and manage the company's upcoming restructuring, which Apple said will include the elimination of programs and positions. Apple did not specify which programs would be eliminated. However, it said the restructuring would begin in early March.
